newsitem.title: USA: Boeing shareholder proposal loses narrowly.
newsitem.headline: Boeing shareholder proposal loses narrowly.

text.p: Boeing Co shareholders Monday narrowly defeated a proposal recommending that directors be elected annually rather than every three years.

A narrow majority of 50.6 percent supported Boeing management on the issue and voted against annual elections, while 48 percent backed the shareholder proposal and about 1.4 percent abstained, according to results read at the company's annual meeting.
Although the proposal was only a recommendation, Boeing chairman and chief executive officer Phil Condit said executives would consider the issue again.
A proposal to amend the company's bylaws would be required to change the method of election, and that would require a 75 percent vote.
Other shareholder proposals did not fare so well.
A proposal asking the board to adopt "basic human rights criteria" for its dealings with China won support from only four percent of shares voted, with 87 percent opposing.
Similarly a proposal seeking new criteria on military contracts was supported by about four percent of shares voted, with 91 percent opposed.
